What Zelda analyzed The work behind this report — counted, not estimated. 12 Pages analyzed 12 Sections searched 2 Categories analyzed Business Model & Growth Analysis Insufficient disclosed data to describe the business model. No revenue model, pricing structure, customer type, or growth driver was extracted from the document. The only disclosed operating indicators are the self-reported traction figures of 140,000+ bots and 500M messages [S1, S2], contextualised to a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16,' which suggest platform-scale usage but do not indicate whether ManyChat charges users, takes a revenue share, or operates on another model. All business model dimensions — monetisation mechanism, customer segment, unit economics, and expansion strategy — are gaps in the extracted evidence. Information Readiness Score: 10/100 Present: • Stage (Series A, profile) [P1] • Sector (Software, profile) [P2] • reported by Pitch Deck Hunt funding raised: $23.1M [S3] • Self-reported traction metrics as of an Apr-16 slide context: 140,000+ bots, 500M messages [S1, S2] Needs Validation: • Funding amount, date, and investor identity [C1] • Traction figures (bots, messages) with independent confirmation [C2, C3] • Revenue, burn, and unit economics • Problem statement and product description • Market size and competitive landscape • Team composition and credentials • Business model and monetisation mechanism • Risk factors disclosed by the company Next evidence to supply: Audited or accountant-reviewed financials showing revenue, gross margin, and burn rate, together with a cap table confirming the funding history. Supported Points • Pitch Deck Hunt lists $23.1M raised [S3]; while unverified, this is a specific figure associated with a named narrator rather than a round number estimate. • The company states, on a slide contextualised to April 2016, 140,000+ bots created and 500M messages sent [S1, S2], indicating material platform activity at that point in time, subject to independent confirmation. Open Concerns • The two core traction claims — 140,000+ bots and 500M messages [S1, S2] — are self-reported and unverified [C2, C3]; without independent confirmation it is unknown whether these figures reflect unique active bots, cumulative totals, or another definition, which is material to understanding platform health. • The $23.1M raised figure [S3] is undated, narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt rather than a primary source, and was checked without result [C1]; the timing, composition, and current availability of these funds remain unknown. • No revenue, burn, or unit economics data was extracted, making it impossible to assess the company's financial sustainability or the efficiency of its growth. • No product, business model, team, or market information was extracted; the gaps collectively mean that the fundamental investment thesis — what ManyChat does, for whom, and how it earns money — cannot be evaluated from the available evidence. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece is a revenue and cost schedule — ideally accountant-reviewed — covering at minimum the twelve months to the deck date, showing monthly recurring revenue, gross margin, and burn rate. This alone would allow the traction figures [S1, S2] to be interpreted in the context of actual monetisation and would anchor assessment of the $23.1M funding figure (per Pitch Deck Hunt) [S3] against remaining runway.
